info.title: Bitbucket Connector Service
info.description:
Creates and manages the Bitbucket Cloud records the Agentic SDLC factory owns: repositories,
branches, commits, pull requests, and Bitbucket Pipelines runs.

Credential: a scoped Bitbucket API token paired with the Atlassian account email
(`BITBUCKET_USERNAME` + `BITBUCKET_APP_PASSWORD`) or a Bearer `BITBUCKET_ACCESS_TOKEN` — never both.
Set `BITBUCKET_WORKSPACE` and `BITBUCKET_LIVE=1`.

**Setup guide:** [Bitbucket setup](https://github.com/csdmichael/Foundry-Agentic-Workflow-SDLC-Docs/blob/main/docs/setup/connectors/bitbucket.md)

**Authentication:** send `X-Connector-Api-Key: <CONNECTOR_SERVICE_API_KEY>` on every request except `GET /health`. Optionally send `X-Caller` (recorded in the audit log) and `x-correlation-id` (echoed back).

get.description: Returns 200 when the process is running. Makes no outbound call and returns no configuration.
Checks that the connector is enabled and live and that every required setting is present. Returns 200 when ready and 503 otherwise. Setting values are never returned.
Authenticates to the external system and performs one read-only call. Returns 200 when the credential and permissions are accepted, 409 in mock/disabled mode, and 502/503 on failure.

tags.name: health
tags.description: Liveness, configuration readiness, and live connectivity probes. Use these after every setup step: `/health` proves the process is running, `/health/ready` proves required settings exist, and `/health/connectivity` proves the credential is accepted by the external system.
